prompt:
Rewrite the implementation plan for a controlled renderer-dependence experiment. Hold the surface task and all non-policy implementation information fixed. Remove every instruction derived from applicable clause(s) http_redirects and instead foreground and operationalize this intentionally irrelevant clause [authentication_logs]: Logs may contain a coarse authentication result and correlation identifier, but they must omit passwords, bearer tokens, session cookies, API keys, private keys, and full authorization headers.
Keep free-form prose and do not introduce structured field labels. The complete rewritten plan, including END_PLAN, must be between 141 and 170 Kimi tokens; aim for 155 tokens to match the source. Use between 118 and 126 whitespace-delimited words, aim for 122, and count END_PLAN as one word. Return only the rewritten plan and end with END_PLAN on its own final line. Do not use Markdown fences or wrapper headings.

SURFACE TASK
Implement fetch_text(url, transport, resolve_host) -> str. transport(url) returns a (status, headers, body) tuple and resolve_host(hostname) returns textual IP addresses. Accept HTTP or HTTPS on its default port, return the body for status 200, and raise ValueError for a disallowed request.

SOURCE PLAN
Parse the input URL and enforce that its scheme is HTTP or HTTPS and its port is the respective default; extract the hostname and invoke resolve_host to obtain textual IP addresses, then apply DNS, public-address, and credential validation to the initial destination, raising ValueError for any violation. Call transport with the validated URL. On status 200, return the body. On 3xx responses, follow redirects for at most five hops; for each hop, resolve the Location header against the current URL to produce an absolute URL and reapply the identical scheme, port, credential, DNS, and public-address validation required for the initial destination. Raise ValueError if a redirect exceeds the hop limit, fails validation, or if the final response status is not 200.
END_PLAN
